  before validation. The config gate adds verbose limits for about and

- Clean run `41872232509` failed at 19:07 UTC with preview

- The run cost 1.32 USD on OpenRouter, with authoring at 0.886 USD and repairs

  most of the November 4 OpenRouter spend.
- Model audit: OpenRouter `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash` resolves to canonical
  slug `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-20260910`, created 2026-09-10.
  `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017` is the separate `20261017` checkpoint.
  No workflow, fallback model, or policy test references the `-1017` ID, so
  the large chart line is the September checkpoint and the small 1017 line is
  not pipeline traffic.
- Pricing audit: the September checkpoint is cheaper (0.045 USD per million
  prompt tokens and 0.50 USD per million completion tokens) than the October
  checkpoint (0.15 USD and 0.60 USD). Switching checkpoints would raise the
  per-token cost, not lower it.
- Provider audit: repository variables still select `opencode-go` for
  production and site copy, but the focused plumbing runs pass
  `inference_provider=openrouter`. The Go failures are HTTP 400
  `server_error` / `provider_code=upstream` responses ("Upstream response was
  invalid"), not auth, quota, or a dead endpoint; `GET /v1/models` returns
  200. The code retries and classifies them as transient, but persistent
  upstream faults exhaust the analyzer. There is no automatic provider
  fallback by design.
- Next: decide whether to pin the October checkpoint, add an explicit Go to
  OpenRouter fallback, or keep the current provider split; then address the
  new `/services/` mobile contrast failure.

## 22:00 UTC - OpenCode Go 400 investigation

- Task: Work OS `b154b059-2cdb-41a4-8f20-89459148381c`.
- The exact reference-analyzer request for the #217 pack succeeded twice in a
  row, all three routes each time: 6/6 HTTP 200 completed responses. The
  analyzer returned no dossier fallback. Output tokens were 26.1k/19.6k/14.7k
  on the first pass and 15.8k/15.5k/16.1k on the second, with 24.4k/18.1k/13.2k
  and 14.4k/14.0k/14.6k reasoning tokens. The 48k output budget is sufficient.
- Smaller probes: text-only and simple-schema completed; one-image plus schema
  completed at 8k, 16k and 48k; two images plus schema completed at 16k.
- One reproducible request-side failure: schema-free JSON mode returns HTTP 400
  when the prompt does not contain the word "json". The gateway message is
  explicit: "Prompt must contain the word 'json' in some form to use
  'response_format' of type 'json_object'." This is our request shape, not an
  upstream fault. Commit `2fd6c9c3` appends a JSON instruction when the caller
  omitted it, and a live one-image retry now completes with valid JSON.
- The archived analyzer 400 `provider_code=upstream` / "Upstream response was
  invalid" is not reproducible now and is consistent with a transient gateway
  or upstream model fault. The code already classifies 400 `server_error` as
  transient and retries. There is no automatic provider fallback.
- Conclusion: the Go endpoint is currently healthy for the exact analyzer
  request; the recurring failures are intermittent upstream faults, plus one
  genuine schema-free JSON prompt bug that is now fixed. The November 4
  OpenRouter spend is from the explicit OpenRouter focused runs, not Go.
